lens: REUSE-FIRST: lift sentinel's proven engine code (audit chain, identifier validators, name normalization + matcher, six typed rule kinds, explainable risk factors, four-eyes case workflow with allowed_actions, typed-explanation API pattern, testcontainers harness, ruff/ty/basedpyright/vulture CI gates, multi-stage Dockerfile, React/shadcn console) into a multi-tenant modular monolith. Each sentinel file lands exactly once, in its final module, already generalized for tenant_id + policy packs, so nothing is ported twice. Only what sentinel structurally lacks is new: tenancy/RLS/encryption, outbox + Postgres job/workflow runner, ports for deferred infra, journeys + connector SDK, KYB graph, reportable-event capture, the reporting engine (Formato 41 TXT + LFPIORPI aviso XML) and the compliance calendar.
summary: One Python package `kycaml` (FastAPI + Pydantic + SQLAlchemy + Alembic on Postgres 17) deployed as two processes from one image: `kycaml serve` (API + console) and `kycaml worker` (outbox dispatcher, Postgres job queue, step-table workflow runner, cron schedules). Infrastructure follows the user's Postgres-first decision: RLS per tenant with `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id`, an `outbox` table with an in-process dispatcher, a `job`/`workflow_run` queue using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, an in-memory screening index rebuilt from Postgres list tables, a local-or-S3 object store and a local key provider wrapping per-tenant DEKs. Kafka, Temporal, OpenSearch, Redis, ClickHouse and KMS are later adapters behind nine ports defined in `platform/`. Country rules are data: `policy-packs/MX/ITF-IFPE/v1.yaml` first, `MX/LFPIORPI-AVI/v1.yaml` second, resolved by a strictest-merge resolver and frozen as `policy_snapshot` rows on every decision (10-f00 §4, 07-data-model §9). The full Mexico launch (delivery-plan Sprints 0–8) is decomposed into 11 sequential sub-projects, ~36.5 weeks for one developer with an AI agent (vs. ~85 eng-weeks for the planned squad; the saving comes from sentinel reuse, no cloud/Kafka/Temporal/OpenSearch build-out, mock vendors and no native mobile SDKs). Build order is kernel → policy/units/calendar/party → lists & screening → risk → cases & console → KYC onboarding → KYB → monitoring & captures → reporting (Formato 41 + aviso XML) → compliance calendar → hardening. The earliest end-to-end demo (screen → hit → case → four-eyes → freeze playbook → audit verify, two tenants isolated) is possible after SP-05; the full sandbox onboarding demo (M2 equivalent) after SP-06; the full report-and-file demo (M4 equivalent) after SP-09. Sentinel code is mapped file by file to its destination, with the exact generalization each file needs.

ports.name: EventBus (transactional outbox)
methods: publish(envelope: Event) -> None  # inserts into outbox inside the caller's transaction; envelope = id, type 'screening.match.created.v1', source, tenant_id, subject, time, policy_version_id, correlation_id, data (ids only, no PII)
subscribe(event_type: str, handler: Callable[[Event], None], consumer: str) -> None
dispatch_pending(batch: int = 200) -> int  # worker loop; at-least-once; handler success recorded in event_consumption(consumer, event_id) for idempotency
replay(from: datetime, types: list[str], tenant_id: UUID | None) -> int
ports.mvp_adapter: PostgresOutboxBus: `outbox` table (10-f00 §7.1) polled by the worker with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, handlers invoked in-process in the same worker, `event_consumption` ledger for idempotency, dead-letter after N attempts visible in console; webhook fan-out is one subscriber that writes webhook_delivery rows (HMAC-signed, exponential retry 24h).
ports.later_adapter: KafkaBus: Debezium CDC (or the same poller) publishes outbox rows to Kafka topics party/screening/risk/txn/alerts/case/report/lists/audit; subscribers become consumer groups; same handler signatures; event_consumption stays for exactly-once effects.

ports.name: JobQueue + WorkflowRunner (durable steps)
methods: enqueue(kind: str, payload: dict, run_at: datetime | None, idempotency_key: str | None, max_attempts: int = 8) -> JobId
claim(worker_id: str, kinds: list[str], limit: int) -> list[Job]  # SKIP LOCKED, lease with heartbeat
complete(job_id) / fail(job_id, error, retry_at: datetime | None)
schedule(name: str, cron: str, kind: str, payload: dict, tz: str) -> None  # list ingestion, re-screen, period close, obligations generator, unit fetchers
start_workflow(definition: str, input: dict, business_key: str) -> RunId  # OnboardingWorkflow, KybWorkflow, ReportRunWorkflow, FreezePlaybook, RescoreAll, SimulateRule
signal(run_id, name: str, payload: dict) -> None  # capture_submitted, review_decided, approval_granted
advance(run_id) -> StepResult  # executes next idempotent step keyed (run_id, step_id, attempt); timers via run_at
get_run(run_id) -> WorkflowRun  # status, current step, history for the console
ports.mvp_adapter: PostgresJobQueue (`job`, `job_schedule` tables) and StepTableWorkflowRunner (`workflow_run`, `workflow_step` tables): workflows are declared as pure step graphs (list of step functions + transitions + timeouts) executed by the worker; steps load/decrypt data themselves and pass ids only; abandonment timers are jobs with run_at.
ports.later_adapter: TemporalWorkflowRunner: each step graph becomes a @workflow.defn whose activities are the same step functions; signals map 1:1; payload codec for encryption; the job queue stays on Postgres or moves to Temporal schedules.

ports.name: ScreeningIndex
methods: index_version(list_version_id: UUID, entries: Iterable[IndexedEntry]) -> None  # IndexedEntry = entry_id, list_kind, names_norm[], phonetic_keys[], ids{type:value}, dob_years[], countries[], gender
retire_version(list_version_id) -> None
index_private(tenant_id: UUID, private_list_id: UUID, entries) -> None  # tenant-scoped shard
index_customers(tenant_id: UUID, parties: Iterable[IndexedName]) -> None  # for reverse/delta screening
candidates(query: NormalizedSubject, scope: Scope(list_kinds, tenant_id, include_private), top_k: int = 50) -> list[CandidateRef]  # recall stage only; scoring stays in Python
reverse_candidates(changed: Iterable[IndexedEntry], tenant_id: UUID, top_k: int) -> list[(party_id, entry_id)]
stats() -> IndexStats  # sizes, versions loaded, memory
ports.mvp_adapter: InMemoryScreeningIndex: sentinel's Screener generalized; built at worker/API startup from list_entry + private_list_entry + person.full_name_norm in Postgres, refreshed on lists.version.published; blocking by rapidfuzz process.extract over normalized aliases plus a phonetic-key dict and an ID hash map; per-tenant private shards and customer-name shards; target p95 < 300 ms at ≤ 500k aliases.
ports.later_adapter: OpenSearchScreeningIndex (ICU folding, beider_morse es/pt, edge n-grams, keyword ids; shared index + per-tenant indices or filtered aliases) or yente logic-v2 as a shadow second opinion; same candidates()/reverse_candidates() contract.

risks.risk: Solo capacity: ~36.5 weeks of planned work against a squad plan of ~85 eng-weeks; regulatory dates (Acuerdo 115 in force 2026-11-30, new aviso XML mandatory 2027-06-01) do not move.
risks.mitigation: Strict exit criteria per sub-project and a pre-agreed cut list in priority order: KYB hosted business flow and LLM extraction (SP-07), rule simulation UI (SP-08), board pack (SP-10), model simulation UI (SP-04). Sentinel code lands first in each module so demos exist early; re-estimate after SP-03 and SP-06 and re-baseline.

risks.risk: In-memory screening index limits: memory and startup time grow with lists (OpenSanctions PEPs ≈ 2M entities) and with per-tenant customer-name shards.
risks.mitigation: MVP scope is sanctions + SAT 69-B + LPB + a bounded PEP subset; index built from Postgres with lazy per-tenant shards; measure at 500k and 2M aliases in SP-11; the ScreeningIndex port keeps the candidates()/reverse_candidates() contract so OpenSearch (or yente shadow mode) is a drop-in adapter.

risks.risk: Postgres as outbox, job queue, aggregate store and sync-decision backend may not meet T1 peaks (500 tx/s) or the 100 ms p99 decide target.
risks.mitigation: Batch ingest, SKIP LOCKED claims, monthly partitions, one indexed read on the decide path, worker horizontal scaling; load test at 2× peak in SP-11 with explicit gates (p99 > 100 ms → Redis hot-aggregate adapter; sustained > 15k events/s or outbox lag → Kafka adapter), both behind existing ports.

risks.risk: Formato 41 and aviso specifications have gaps: UIF catalogs (tipo_alerta, networks), 2027 XSDs not downloadable, SITI authentication and acuse format unverified, layouts for FX-cash/international-transfer/VA reports behind logins.
risks.mitigation: Definitions, code tables and XSDs are data with valid_from/valid_to; build from the public Formato 41 resolution and avi.xsd with golden files; keep definition slots for the missing layouts; validate with the design partner in SITI QA / SAT test before pilot; monthly regulatory review updates the data, not the engine.

risks.risk: Typed rule kinds (sentinel) may be less expressive than the Notion rule DSL for some typologies or future packs, forcing a rewrite.
risks.mitigation: Kinds declare their aggregates up front (same state model as the DSL design), captures and tier limits are first-class kinds, and rule definitions are versioned JSON; the DSL compiler is an additive extension that targets the same AggregateReader and RuleHit, so existing rules and evidence survive.

risks.risk: RLS correctness with connection pooling and background workers: a missing SET LOCAL, a BYPASSRLS role or a non-tenant FK can leak data across tenants.
risks.mitigation: Session hook refuses to open tenant-scoped sessions without a context, worker jobs carry tenant_id and set it per job, the isolation harness auto-discovers tables in CI, and composite (tenant_id, id) FKs are mandatory before the first production tenant (SP-11).

risks.risk: Fuzzy name matching needs readable normalized names, in tension with field-level encryption (07-data-model §9 rule 4 open decision).
risks.mitigation: Store full_name_norm (normalized tokens, no raw name) readable only by the matcher DB role, keep raw names encrypted, and keep the per-tenant customer-name shard in memory; document the guarantee in the security pack; revisit if a partner requires option (b).

risks.risk: A home-grown step-table workflow runner (instead of Temporal) can accumulate subtle bugs in retries, timers and signals.
risks.mitigation: Keep it minimal and generic (one table pair, idempotent steps keyed by (run_id, step_id, attempt), timers as jobs), write workflow definitions as pure step graphs with contract tests (crash/restart, duplicate signal, timeout), and keep the WorkflowRunner port so the Temporal adapter is a mechanical port.

risks.risk: Mock-only vendor connectors: real Incode/RENAPO/INE response shapes, latencies and failure modes will differ, and the INE path for non-bank fintechs needs a legal opinion.
risks.mitigation: Vendor-agnostic DocResult/CheckResult contracts with calibration versions, recorded-response contract tests ready for sandbox credentials, assurance levels so launch at A3 (RENAPO + document + liveness) with INE as A4 add-on; connectors are the last thing to swap and touch no business logic.

risks.risk: Second pack (MX/LFPIORPI-AVI) doubles reporting and calendar surface (SAT portal XML, informe en ceros, 24-hour avisos from 2027-06-01) for a solo developer.
risks.mitigation: Share the engine (captures, runs, approvals, filing, calendar) and keep the AV-specific work to one definition family (AVI) and one obligation seed; other activities are new YAML definitions after GA.

risks.risk: Spanish-first UI and Mexican regulatory wording drift across a long build.
risks.mitigation: i18n scaffold in SP-01, all new strings keyed from the start, a native-speaker compliance review of templates/narratives before pilot (SP-11).
